summary: Ten comment-endorsed discoveries spanning agent workflows, Rust scripting, monitoring, desktop customization, books, television, architecture, and low-tech gardening.
telegram_footer: 10 items surfaced | 30/30 prior-day front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: Paseo
items.summary: A desktop and mobile interface for coding agents, praised for phone control and diffs.
items.why_included: A first-hand recommendation describes an entire team switching within a week, warranting resurfacing after the cooldown.
items.evidence: sergiotapia recommends Paseo, praising its diff view and phone control of home-hosted agents, and reports rapid team adoption.

evidence_sources.author: sergiotapia
evidence_sources.excerpt: It works really well, has the nice code diff view which what I used to open vs code for, and it lets you drive from your phone. All the beefy work happens on my machine at home with big hardware and .env secrets, etc. And from my phone I'm able to run multiple threads with multiple models/thinking modes. I think a testament of how useful it is, is everybody on my team switched over to Paseo pretty much in a week.

items.name: OpenSpec
items.source_story_title: How I Fight AI Brain Fry
items.summary: A spec-driven workflow for AI coding, keeping proposals, task checklists, and reviews traceable.
items.why_included: A concrete review workflow offers a practical response to agent context switching and merits resurfacing after the cooldown.
items.evidence: driverdan uses OpenSpec with PRs at proposal, apply, and archive stages, and values its retrospective specifications and task checklist.

evidence_sources.author: driverdan
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use the OpenSpec[1] workflow with PRs at each step, proposal, apply, archive. I have the LLM do those steps but I review the results and have it make changes as needed. OpenSpec specs make it easy to look back at what it was supposed to do if necessary, including a checklist of tasks.

items.name: scheme-rs
items.source_story_title: Clj.rs – a Clojure dialect implemented in Rust
items.summary: An embeddable Scheme implementation for Rust, praised for flexible scripting and hot reloading.
items.why_included: A first-hand endorsement surfaces a useful alternative beyond the submitted Clojure project.
items.evidence: sshine calls scheme-rs a favorite crate, uses it whenever dynamic scripting is needed, and praises flexible hot reloading.

evidence_sources.author: sshine
evidence_sources.excerpt: I'm already a big fan of the scheme-rs crate. I use it any time I need a dynamic scripting language. It allows for more flexible hot-reloading of parts of a program.

items.name: VictoriaMetrics
items.source_story_title: What I run on my $10 USD OpenStick homelab
items.summary: A time-series monitoring database, praised for a small footprint at home and work.
items.why_included: A user running hundreds of work servers provides specific praise for storage efficiency.
items.evidence: InsidiousWombat uses VictoriaMetrics at home and across a few hundred work servers, calling it excellent, small, and economical on disk.

evidence_sources.author: InsidiousWombat
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use it for a while now both for work (few hundred servers) and for home stuff and it is excellent, small and low on disk storage (yes that sounds like PR, no, it is not, I'm just very happy user)

items.name: Dux Modular Shell
items.source_story_title: Dux: Free, open-source Wayland desktop shell with file manager and theming
items.summary: A customizable Wayland desktop shell, praised by a daily user for QML widgets.
items.why_included: The submitted project has an independent daily-use endorsement with a concrete customization benefit.
items.evidence: mariocesar uses Dux daily and is happy with a workflow built around Niri and custom QML widgets, while noting a learning curve from GNOME Shell.

evidence_sources.author: mariocesar
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use it daily. There was a learning curve since I was used to GNOME Shell, but Niri and the ability to build my own widgets with QML ended up being the killer features for me. I've built several custom widgets and small apps, and I'm happy with my workflow

items.name: The Winter Fortress
items.source_story_title: Uranium cubes reveal why the German nuclear project failed
items.summary: A nonfiction book about Norwegian commandos sabotaging the Nazis' heavy-water supply.
items.why_included: An emphatic rereader recommendation adds a concrete book discovery to a science-history thread.
items.evidence: mauvehaus calls The Winter Fortress one of their favorite books and describes repeatedly rereading its Norwegian sabotage story.

evidence_sources.author: mauvehaus
evidence_sources.excerpt: Since Norsk Hydro was mentioned in the article, I have to mention in turn one of my favorite books ever: The Winter Fortress by Neil Bascomb. It's the true story of the Norwegian commando sabotage of the heavy water plant. Short version: after a failed attempt by the English, some locals who'd fled to England and received training parachuted in, blew it up, and then skied to neutral Sweden. Legends, the lot of them: they froze their balls off and didn't have enough to eat, but they pulled it off. Every time I re-read it, it makes me want to take up nordic skiing.

items.name: Person of Interest
items.summary: An AI-surveillance crime drama that inspired a commenter to pursue an AI career.
items.why_included: A personal account connects the show's appeal to a real study and career decision.
items.evidence: scrollaway credits Person of Interest with inspiring an AI study and career path; ghaff enjoyed it initially but lost interest over time.

evidence_sources.author: scrollaway
evidence_sources.excerpt: I watched the show in 2014 and it drove my interest to study and work in the AI sector (today I run an AI lab, whose name comes from that tv show).

evidence_sources.author: ghaff
evidence_sources.excerpt: I enjoyed it for a bit but it was one of those shows that just didn't grab me after a while.

items.name: Museum Het Schip
items.summary: An Amsterdam School architecture museum, recommended for its guided tour and workers' housing.
items.why_included: A specific, locally accessible museum receives direct tour praise rather than a bare mention.
items.evidence: ggm calls the Het Schip museum tour fantastic and well worth it.

evidence_sources.author: ggm
evidence_sources.excerpt: Bit of a cheat putting Zaanstraat and Hembrugstraat in without noting they're both part of "Het Schip" and basically opposite ends of the same development. The museum tour is fantastic. Well worth it.

items.name: Rietveld Schröderhuis
items.summary: A De Stijl house museum in Utrecht, recommended as a fascinating architecture trip.
items.why_included: A direct recommendation surfaces a distinct architectural destination beyond the submitted Amsterdam School article.
items.evidence: ggm recommends a trip to the Rietveld Schröderhuis, explicitly distinguishing its De Stijl architecture from the Amsterdam School.

evidence_sources.author: ggm
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you like this kind of thing, the Rietveld Schröderhuis in Utrecht is well worth a trip. It's de Stijl not Amsterdam school but also fascinating.

items.name: Ollas
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Vegetable Gardening for Engineers
items.summary: Buried terracotta watering pots that irrigate plants without electronics; a DIY guide is linked.
items.why_included: A successful first-hand low-tech gardening setup offers useful serendipity beyond software.
items.evidence: Joakal reports an efficient, inexpensive, electricity-free olla setup made with terracotta pots and silicone, with irrigation fittings connected to a tank.

evidence_sources.author: Joakal
evidence_sources.excerpt: I found an ancient solution that worked incredibly efficient and required no electricity and far cheaper than spending hundreds on electronics. Ollas. The science is called capillary action. I went a step further as an engineer, and did DIY terracotta pots + silicone. Added a testing stage, of course. Filled pots and sealed it over night. If leaking from seal, more silicone. For filling them up, I used irrigation fittings hooked up to a tank.
